entry.title: Why Fe doping kills photoluminescence in CsPbCl$_3$ but not in CsPbBr$_3$: Role of midgap Fe 3$d$ states and electron-phonon coupling
entry.summary: Understanding the impact of transition-metal doping on the optoelectronic properties of halide perovskite nanocrystals is essential for their rational design in photonic applications. We establish the microscopic origin of photoluminescence (PL) quenching in Fe-doped CsPbCl$_3$ using spin-polarized density functional theory calculations. The emergence of Fe 3$d$ midgap states creates efficient electron-trapping centres that drive nonradiative recombination, accounting for the reduced PL intensity. Extending this analysis to Fe-doped CsPbX$_3$ (X = Cl, Br), we show experimentally that although PL intensity is suppressed in both systems relative to their pristine counterparts, their high-doping behaviour diverges: CsPbCl$_3$ becomes completely non-emissive, whereas CsPbBr$_3$ retains a finite, saturated PL intensity. Despite this contrast, electronic structure calculations reveal nearly identical midgap states in both materials, indicating that electronic effects alone cannot explain the distinct PL responses. Phonon calculations likewise fail to capture this difference. In contrast, electron-phonon coupling calculations based on the deformation potential approach reveal significantly stronger coupling in Fe-doped CsPbCl$_3$, enabling efficient dissipation of electronic excitation energy into lattice vibrations and leading to complete PL quenching. These results identify electron-phonon coupling as the key factor governing halide-dependent PL quenching and provide a unified microscopic framework for dopant-induced nonradiative processes in halide perovskites.

entry.title: Timelike Entanglement Entropy and Renormalization Group Flow Irreversibility
entry.summary: We study holographic $c$-theorems based on timelike entanglement entropy and show that timelike $c$-functions capture irreversible renormalization group (RG) flow. We demonstrate that timelike $c$-functions are applicable to both relativistic and nonrelativistic quantum matter in nematic phases with broken rotational symmetry, and that they remain monotonic along holographic anisotropic RG flows under explicit geometric conditions, thereby passing some of the most stringent consistency tests. We derive the exact flow of the composite timelike $c$-function in general homogeneous anisotropic geometries and establish the $c$-theorem for adiabatic flows. Across all classes of scaling backgrounds examined, consistent with the null energy condition and thermodynamic stability, the monotonicity condition universally reduces to a constraint on a running geometric effective dimension. We further construct a second $c$-function purely from the imaginary part of the timelike entanglement entropy and prove its monotonicity under the local effective-dimension condition, without requiring adiabaticity. For Poincaré-invariant flows, this condition follows directly from the null energy condition. Moreover, we identify a geometric upper bound on the rate of change of the timelike $c$-functions, which constrains how rapidly effective degrees of freedom can be coarse-grained. Our results suggest that capturing RG irreversibility in nonrelativistic flows requires observables that are intrinsically sensitive to the temporal direction. The applicability of holographic $c$-theorems is thus extended to highly nontrivial RG flows and points toward a new information-theoretic diagnostic of holographic RG dynamics.

entry.title: Black hole thermodynamics and KK photon quantum corrections in 2D effective dilaton gravity
entry.summary: We study black hole thermodynamics using a two-dimensional effective theory obtained by dimensional reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For spherically symmetric charged black holes, the resulting dilaton gravity has a nonlinear potential that reproduces the semiclassical phase structure of four-dimensional AdS black holes, including the Hawking--Page transition and the small/large Reissner--Nordström--AdS black hole transition. This shows that the two-dimensional theory before taking the near-horizon and near-extremal limits captures non-extremal thermodynamics beyond the Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity regime. We also include electromagnetic Kaluza--Klein modes on the internal sphere and integrate them out to derive the one-loop effective dilaton gravity. At leading order in the derivative expansion, these corrections appear as constant shifts in the black hole entropy and in the effective charge parameter of the dilaton potential. Therefore, the semiclassical phase structure is not qualitatively modified within this leading local approximation.

entry.title: Unveiling Topological Fusion in Quantum Hall Systems from Microscopic Principles
entry.summary: Establishing the fusion rules of anyonic quasiparticles in fractional quantum Hall fluids is essential for understanding their underlying topological order. Building on the conjecture that key topological properties are encoded in the ''DNA'' of candidate many-body wave functions - that is, the pattern of dominant orbital occupations restricted to a finite number of lowest Landau levels - we propose a combinatorial framework that derives these fusion rules directly from microscopic data. By extending Schrieffer's counting argument and introducing classes of topological excitations, our framework provides a unified route to the fusion rules for both Abelian and non-Abelian excitations. This approach elucidates the emergence of topological features from first principles in both fermionic and bosonic systems. In particular, we unveil the previously unknown fusion rules of the Hafnian fluid.

entry.title: Gravitational Waves from Magnetically Confined Mountains on Accreting White Dwarfs
entry.summary: We propose fast-spinning, magnetic white dwarfs in binary systems as promising sources of continuous gravitational waves for future space-based detectors. The aim of this work is to determine the maximum ellipticities and gravitational wave amplitudes achievable by magnetically confined mountains accreted on the star's magnetic poles, and to assess their detectability against predicted sensitivity curves. Self-consistent magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium simulations are used to characterize the structure of the accreted mountain. A parametric search is then performed on these simulations to determine the maximum mass values that can be confined by the star's magnetic field. The stellar ellipticity $\varepsilon$ grows nearly linearly with accreted mass $M_{\rm a}$ up to a maximum, and was found to scale as $\varepsilon_{\rm max} \simeq 1.6\times10^{-2}T_5^{-2} B_{*,8}^{2}$, while the maximum gravitational wave amplitude as $h_{\rm 0, max} \simeq 1.2\times10^{-23}T_5^{-2} B_{*,8}^{2}$, where $T_5$ represents the temperature of the mountain in units of $10^5 \mathrm{K}$ and $B_{*,8}$ represents the star's polar magnetic field intensity in units of $10^8 \mathrm{G}$. Across a representative range of source inclinations, distances and spin periods, magnetically confined mountains on white dwarfs can generate continuous gravitational waves detectable by future space-based interferometers. BBO and DECIGO can probe diverse configurations, whereas LISA, TianQin, and Taiji require highly magnetized systems. Applications to known fast-spinning white dwarfs indicate that cooler accreted mountains favor detectability.

entry.title: Late Epoch Infrared Spectroscopy and Two-Component 3D Photoionization Modeling of Classical Nova V5668 Sgr
entry.summary: V5668 Sgr is an Fe II classical nova (CN) that exploded on 15 March 2015. We present near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy of the ejecta from the Mt. Abu observatory which exhibits emission lines of species H, He, N, S, Ti, and Si. We also present SOFIA (+FORCAST) spectroscopy which shows two forbidden emission lines, [Ne II] at 12.8 $μ$m and [O IV] at 25.9 $μ$m, as well as two emission features attributed to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) at 6.2 $μ$m and 11.3 $μ$m. 1D Cloudy photoionization simulations require two components to model the system, which suggests a multifaceted, morphologically complex ejecta. The 1D simulations also reveal He, N, Ne, S, Ti, Si, and O chemical abundances elevated above fiducial solar levels. 3D pyCloudy photoionization emission profiles visualize the ejecta and elucidate the system's complex composition.

entry.title: Initial Data Gluing for Asymptotically Hyperbolic Spacetimes
entry.summary: We give a new proof of Corvino-Schoen-type gluing, also known as gluing up to linear obstructions, for asymptotically hyperbolic spacetimes satisfying appropriate smallness conditions in arbitrary dimension. The results retrieve and improve on previous known smallness requirements on initial data to conduct such gluing, including the work of Chrusciél and Delay. Our technique is highly versatile and well-suited for gluing results in highly anisotropic geometric settings.

entry.title: Constraining the Inner Dark Matter Profiles of Strong-Lensing Galaxy Clusters
entry.summary: We present mass modeling of three strong lensing galaxy clusters found in the Dark Energy Survey utilizing Hubble Space Telescope imaging for lens modeling, and complementary constraints from Chandra X-ray observations. All three clusters are relaxed and have giant arc or ring lens structures ideal for constraints on the dark matter distribution. The strong lens modeling and X-ray temperatures yield consistent total cluster mass estimates. We find these clusters have best-fit X-ray temperatures of $2.7 - 6.2$ keV and total masses of M$_{200} = (1-6) \times 10^{14} M_{\odot}$. Our lens models parameterize dark matter distribution with a generalized Navarro-Frenk-White (GNFW) density profile. While the GNFW profile allows the inner dark matter slope to vary, we find in all cases that the inner slopes are consistent with the standard NFW density profile $γ^{DM} = 1$. The X-ray surface brightness distributions for all three clusters are generally symmetric with no significant substructure, supporting the conclusion that these are relaxed clusters. In addition, we find generally low values of the external shear magnitude with median values ranging $|γ^{ext}| = 0.04-0.09$ and consistent with zero for two of the clusters.

entry.title: Clock--WEP Tests of String-Derived Dilaton and Modulus Sectors
entry.summary: String compactifications and runaway-dilaton models can contain light scalar directions. Motion along these directions changes gauge couplings, the QCD scale, quark masses, and Yukawa parameters. A given string-derived sector then predicts low-energy slopes. Its gauge kinetic functions, matter-metric or Yukawa slopes, source charge, scalar trajectory, and scalar range determine a Damour--Donoghue weak-equivalence-principle (WEP) vector and a clock-drift vector. The fit assumes one long-range scalar or an aligned multi-field direction. With that assumption, WEP tests and secular clock drifts probe related projections of the same scalar-slope vector. The minimal two-charge Damour--Donoghue fit uses Ti--Pt MICROSCOPE, Be--Ti torsion-balance, and $^{85}$Rb--$^{87}$Rb atom-interferometer data, then adds the Yb$^+$ E3/E2 secular $α$-drift row. The WEP-only fit gives $D_{\hat m}=(-6.06\pm34.91)\times10^{-12}$ and $D_e=(8.80\pm46.46)\times10^{-12}$, with correlation $-0.99958$. The clock input is $\dotα/α=1.0(1.1)\times10^{-18}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. It matches the WEP marginal reach when $|ζ|=2.37\times10^{-8}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, with $ζ=\dot\varphi/α_E$. For the benchmark $\dot\varphi=ξH_0$ and $α_E=10^{-3}α_0$, this gives $ξ/α_0\simeq0.34$. A model becomes testable after it supplies $r=D_{\hat m}/D_e$, the scalar amplitude, and $ζ$. The Damour--Piazza--Veneziano runaway-dilaton estimate lies near $η\sim10^{-12}$ for order-unity $n=2$ parameters, well above the MICROSCOPE-level WEP scale. In the representative-isotope two-charge model, a MICROSCOPE-level Be--Ti-like row would reduce the long WEP axis by a factor $27.8$; a repeated Ti--Pt-like row would barely change it. The calculation tests compactification-level predictions for string-derived dilaton or modulus sectors after the model supplies its low-energy data.

entry.title: Logarithmic corrections to the entropy of near-extremal black holes in New Massive Gravity
entry.summary: We study the one-loop correction to the entropy of near-extremal black holes in three-dimensional massive gravity at the special point where the theory exhibits a unique maximally symmetric vacuum and non-constant curvature hairy black holes can achieve extremality even in the static case. Focusing on the near-horizon AdS$_2\times S^1$ geometry, we evaluate the contribution of boundary graviton modes that become exact zero modes in the extremal limit. We show that the resulting one-loop partition function generates logarithmic corrections to the semiclassical entropy, providing a new extension to higher-curvature gravity of what has been recently obtained for near-extremal black holes in General Relativity.

entry.title: Fate of Quantum Scars and Chaos-Assisted Tunneling under Dissipation
entry.summary: Quantum scars enable memory and recurrent dynamics, but their fate under dissipation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that distinct quantum scars can respond qualitatively differently to the same dissipative channel. We consider a collective spin model coupled to a lossy cavity and, guided by its classical limit, identify scars associated with two unstable structures: a saddle point on a dissipation-free invariant manifold with vanishing cavity field and an unstable superradiant fixed point with finite photon occupation. The former is immune to photon loss in the classical limit and exhibits persistent quantum revivals, whereas the latter couples directly to the dissipative channel, but exhibits slow dynamics. Remarkably, the superradiant scar also supports chaos-assisted quantum tunneling between two symmetry-related, macroscopically distinct semiclassical configurations, despite the presence of dissipation. Our results identify an experimentally accessible setting for exploring dissipative scarring and chaos-assisted tunneling in cavity QED.

entry.title: Constraining Ultralight Dark Matter in Dynamical Dark Energy Cosmologies
entry.summary: We investigate the cosmological implications of scalar-field dark matter (SFDM) in a dynamical dark energy framework, extending previous analyses that considered SFDM within the standard $Λ$CDM cosmological model. We consistently implement the scenario at both the background and linear perturbation levels. We perform Bayesian parameter inference using Planck CMB measurements, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, and Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae to constrain the model parameter space. Our theoretical predictions show that lighter scalar-field masses produce increasingly strong scale-dependent suppression of matter fluctuations and more pronounced modifications to the CMB temperature power spectrum, whereas heavier masses progressively approach the cold dark matter limit. For the SFDM mass, we obtain a one-sided 95\% lower limit of $\log_{10}(m_φ/{\rm eV})>-24.04$ from our main joint analysis. We find that replacing the standard cold dark matter fluid with SFDM does not qualitatively alter the constraints on dynamical dark energy or the evidence for its evolution, including a phantom crossing at low redshifts.

entry.title: A new analytical finding for the Born-Infeld integral potential
entry.summary: A new finding regarding the Born-Infeld potential for short range distances from the charge revealed that its integral form can be almost exact written as the difference between a Coulomb-type potential and a Yukawa-type potential. This allowed for an immediate physical interpretation in terms of classical vacuum polarization and an effective mass. Subsequently, a new U(r) is proposed to cover the entire space. This formulation is then applied to calculate, in a closed manner, the first-order energy shifts in hydrogen-like atoms; a comparison of these shifts with high-precision spectroscopic data provides a model-dependent lower bound for the maximum field intensity parameter b.

entry.title: Accretion Geometry and Variability in QS Telescopii from multi-epoch Observations
entry.summary: We present phase-resolved photometry, spectroscopy, photopolarimetry, and circular spectropolarimetry of the polar QS Telescopii, obtained between 2017 and 2025 using the South African Astronomical Observatory (SAAO) 1.0-m and 1.9-m telescopes, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System (ATLAS) and the Southern African Large Telescope (SALT). From ground-based photometry, we report the first detection of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in QS Tel, with timescales ranging between 2 and 11 minutes. This makes QS Tel one of only seven polars to show QPOs. The average spectra of QS Tel show broad and strong Balmer ($\rm Hδ$, $\rm Hγ$, $\rm Hβ$ and $\rm Hα$) and He\textsc{ii} 4686 Å emission lines, along with weaker emission from He\textsc{i} at (6678\,Å, 5017\,Å, 4921\,Å, 4712\,Å, 4471\,Å, and 4387\,Å) and the Bowen fluorescence complex C\textsc{iii}/N\textsc{iii} at 4650\,Å. For the first time detailed Doppler tomography of the $\rm Hα$ and He\textsc{ii}\,4686\,Å\, lines are presented which reveal emission from the irradiated face of the secondary star, the ballistic stream, the threading region and complex magnetically confined flows. The magnetically confined accretion stream splits into two distinct components coming from the same stream. One component appears near the threading region and the other component is seen along the high velocity in the magnetically confined accretion stream closer to the White Dwarf. Broad band photopolarimetry reveals circular polarisation reaching levels of $+8\%$, however more detailed circular spectropolarimetry shows polarisation ranging from $-10\%$ to $+25\%$, associated with two broad, phase-dependent cyclotron humps centred at $\sim$4800 Å and $\sim$6300 Å, consistent with a magnetic field strength of $\sim$53 MG.

entry.title: Integrable open elliptic Toda chain with boundaries
entry.summary: In this letter we discuss the classical integrable elliptic Toda chain proposed by I. Krichever. Our goal is to construct an open elliptic Toda chain with boundary terms. This is achieved using the factorized form of the Lax matrix and gauge equivalence with the XYZ chain.
entry.arxiv:comment: 13 pages, typos corrected, comments and proofs added

entry.title: On the existence of toric ALE and ALF gravitational instantons
entry.summary: We establish existence and uniqueness results for asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) and asymptotically locally flat (ALF) gravitational instantons. In particular, we prove the existence of a unique, Ricci-flat, toric ALE and ALF gravitational instanton, for every admissible rod structure, that is smooth up to possible conical singularites. We also give an elementary proof that any toric ALE or ALF self-dual instanton is a multi-Eguchi-Hanson or multi-Taub-NUT solution.
entry.arxiv:comment: 21 pages. v2: minor edits, published version

entry.title: Ubiquity of ocular resonances in scattering phenomena
entry.summary: We demonstrate how quantum mechanical scattering off a potential with a characteristic surface generically leads to a family of resonances in the complex momentum plane clustered near a roughly eye-shaped curve centered on the origin and formed by anti-Stokes lines. A particularly interesting class are potentials that are more singular than $1/r^2$ at short distance, where the scattering surface is the separatrix between captured and deflected classical trajectories. These resonances have been recently shown to play an important role in low energy nucleon scattering, and can be related to ``creeping waves'' familiar from classical diffractive scattering and analyzed by means of Regge poles.

entry.title: Neutron Star--Primordial Black Hole Binaries: Dynamical Tides, Resonance Locking, and Gravitational Waves
entry.summary: The orbital evolution of a neutron star and a much lower-mass primordial black hole can differ strikingly from that of typical compact binaries. Dynamical tides, analogous to those in the Solar System's giant planet-moon systems, can accelerate inspiral or induce outspiral, depending on the orbital configuration. We show how gravitational-wave emission mediates this evolution when neutron star modes remain locked in resonance with the orbit. These effects may leave observable signatures in pulsar timing or gravitational waves.

entry.title: Impact of nonlinear electrodynamics on quasinormal modes of rotating black strings
entry.summary: We study massless scalar perturbations of rotating anti-de Sitter black strings sourced by a power-Maxwell field with negative exponent $s$. The charge enters the metric function as $-Qr^{p}$ with $p=2/(1-2s)$, and the case $s=-1/2$ gives a linear term with an algebraic horizon. Since rotation is a local boost of the static string, the rotating spectrum follows exactly from the static one evaluated at a frequency-dependent momentum. We compute the spectrum with the Horowitz-Hubeny series, Chebyshev collocation and time-domain evolution, each implemented in two independent codes and checked against the planar Schwarzschild-AdS limit. The charge acts in two ways. At the reduced charge $\hat q_c=0.72626$ the least damped pair of modes meets on the imaginary axis, so more strongly charged strings ring down without oscillation, and at the endpoint of the branch the spectrum is exactly hypergeometric. At large transverse momentum the distance of the modes from the light cone grows as $k^{1/(1-4s)}$, replacing the $k^{-1/5}$ law of the neutral brane. Rotation continues the exceptional point into a line in the plane of charge and rotation, adds a purely damped axisymmetric tower, and never produces superradiant growth. A near-horizon estimate used earlier for this geometry misses all of these effects.

entry.title: Initial Conditions of Magnetized AGN Accretion Disks from Cloud Capture and Disruption
entry.summary: Accretion onto supermassive black holes (BHs) from the ISM can occur via capture of cold gas 'clouds' (GMCs, clumps, or overdense structures). Unlike material in stellar tidal disruptions or X-ray binaries, or classical Bondi accretion, ISM clouds are strongly magnetized (plasma $β\equiv P_{\rm thermal}/P_{\rm magnetic} \ll 1$), with supersonic turbulence, and cool rapidly. We derive analytic scalings for the initial conditions of accretion disks formed by capture/disruption of such clouds, in three regimes: (1) low-mass BHs ($M_{\rm BH} \ll M_{\rm cl}$), where turbulent Bondi-Hoyle or hierarchical 'leapfrog' growth via sub-cloud encounters dominates; (2) comparable-mass encounters ($M_{\rm BH} \sim M_{\rm cl}$); and (3) massive BHs tidally disrupting small clouds ($M_{\rm BH} \gg M_{\rm cl}$). In each, the resulting disk is predicted to be initially toroidally-magnetically-dominated ($|B_φ| \gg |B_{z}|$, $β\ll 1$), geometrically thick ($H/R \sim 0.1-1$), and gravitationally stable ($Q \gtrsim 1$), with super-sonic, trans-Alfvenic turbulence. These conditions differ qualitatively from those assumed in classical accretion/$α$ disk theory, 'chaotic cold accretion', stellar tidal disruption, or Bondi-Hoyle accretion. At least initially, the toroidal field should be sustained by flux-freezing on timescales shorter than Parker or turbulent resistive losses. We examine how cloud mass spectra drive accretion rate distributions, duty cycles, and fueling rates, with integrated BH growth dominated by clouds of mass comparable to the BH. Given known cosmological evolution, we suggest a scenario linking (a) inefficient growth and wandering BHs in dwarf galaxies, (b) hyper-Eddington growth in little red dots, (c) peak quasar activity in massive gas-rich systems at cosmic noon, and (d) lower-luminosity AGN in gas-poor galaxies at late times.
entry.arxiv:comment: 15 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics. Comments welcome

entry.title: STOKES tables and KY codes
entry.summary: The family of KY codes is an XSPEC-compatible package of fully relativistic models for spectro-polarimetric modeling of X-ray binary systems and active galactic nuclei. Within Kerr space-time, they compute accretion disc line profiles, reflection spectra from discs illuminated by Comptonized coronal radiation, and thermal disc emission including disc-corona interaction and disc self-irradiation. Many of these models include polarimetric computations, and more advanced timing variants compute X-ray, UV and optical reverberation. The primary source of Comptonized X-rays is assumed to be in the lamp-post on-axis or slab above the disc geometry. The KY codes operate at various levels of complexity; some models use analytical approximations for local re-processing, while others rely on detailed numerical tables. For the most accurate treatment of rest-frame re-processing in partially ionized accretion disc atmospheres, the KY codes employ pre-computed spectro-polarimetric tables generated with the STOKES code. These transmission and reflection tables are also designed for standalone use in XSPEC and as inputs to higher-level models beyond KY. The chapter first introduces the STOKES tables in various variants and shows their non-relativistic usage in XSPEC models for (i) an extended source illuminating a distant geometrically thin disc, and (ii) a compact source illuminating a vertically extended equatorial obscurer (e.g., a torus or thick wind). The relativistic KY ray-tracing is then described, followed by an introduction to each KY model. Examples of fits to the IXPE data of X-ray binaries and active galactic nuclei using these models are shown. Together, these models form a comprehensive and publicly available framework for spectro-polarimetric modeling and data fitting of accretion. We provide links to their online repositories.

entry.title: Taub-NUT as gravitational dyon with torsion
entry.summary: We show that the Levi-Civita connection for the Taub-NUT metric is singular on Misner strings and generates an Einstein tensor containing the squares of the delta function. This can be improved by introducing torsion, in which case the Einstein tensor may be interpreted as that of a cosmic string with negative variable tension. Komar flows in Misner strings are generated by torsion, which is therefore responsible for the asymptotic Komar charges. The Taub-NUT metric then appears as a soliton supported by two spin-fluid beams.

entry.title: Topological cones and positively polarizable hyperbolic norms
entry.summary: In the first part of this article, we study linear cones over totally ordered fields. We show that for each such cone there uniquely exists a universal vector space (called its spanned vector space) into which it embeds as a generating convex cone. Moreover, we investigate topologies on cones for which the natural cone operations are continuous, and study how these topologies carry over to the spanned vector space. In the second part, we deal with hyperbolic norms which satisfy a polarization identity and are defined on cones over the real numbers. We show that, under reasonable assumptions, such hyperbolic norms induce a Lorentzian inner product on the spanned vector space. Finally, we establish a link between completeness under the Wick rotation of a Lorentzian inner product and order-theoretic completeness.
entry.arxiv:comment: 25 pages, to appear in Monatshefte Math

entry.title: Factorization in deep inelastic scattering at Björken limit: Reduction to (1+1)D integrable models
entry.summary: We study the small-$x$ behavior of the proton structure function $F_2(x,Q^2)$ using the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data and compare it with exact structure functions obtained in integrable quantum field theories. The data are described by a local power law, $F_2(x,Q^2)=A(Q^2)x^{-γ(Q^2)}$, where the exponent $γ(Q^2)$ increases smoothly with the hard scale. We show that this running exponent is well described by a simple renormalization-group crossover form and is compatible with the illustrative limiting value $C=γ(\infty)\simeq0.431$. This reference belongs to the sine-Gordon power-law universality class among the exactly solvable possibilities and corresponds to the coupling $β^2/π=16/(3-C)\simeq6.23$. The sine-Gordon-constrained fit gives a quantitatively accurate description of the HERA $F_2$ surface, with reduced $χ^2$ close to unity, and is cross-checked with the overlapping final HERA reduced-cross-section data. These results indicate that the small-$x$ growth observed in deep inelastic scattering is naturally organized by a sine-Gordon-type universality class, while the finite-$Q^2$ dependence is controlled by a smooth crossover toward the corresponding asymptotic exponent.

entry.title: Hyperboloidal Initial Data with Prescribed Asymptotic Charges
entry.summary: A novel method is introduced for constructing hyperboloidal initial data with direct analytic control over asymptotic charges prior to solving the Einstein constraint equations. Using the parabolic-hyperbolic formulation of the constraints together with a Fuchsian-analysis-inspired spectral solver, the asymptotic degrees of freedom, which determine infinite towers of asymptotic charges, including the Bondi energy and angular momentum, are used to prescribe the asymptotic behavior of solutions. As a proof of concept, we explicitly construct hyperboloidal initial data for a spinning black hole with Bondi energy $E_B = 2$ and angular momentum $J_B = 1/2$, starting from seed data induced on a hyperboloidal slice of the non-rotating Schwarzschild spacetime with mass $M=1$.

entry.title: Elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda and elliptic Toda chains: classical r-matrix structure and relation to XYZ chain
entry.summary: We discuss the classical elliptic Toda chain introduced by Krichever and the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda chain introduced by Adler, Shabat and Suris. It is shown that these models can be obtained as particular cases of the elliptic Ruijsenaars chain. We explain how the classical $r$-matrix structures are derived for these chains. Also, as a by-product, we prove that the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda chain is gauge equivalent to discrete Landau-Lifshitz model of XYZ type. The elliptic Toda chain is also gauge equivalent to XYZ chain with special values of the Casimir functions at each site.

entry.title: Strong Lensing Tomography: Double and pseudo multi-source plane strong gravitational lensing to constrain dark energy
entry.summary: Tomographic measurements of gravitational lensing with different lens and source redshift distributions contain crucial information about the universe's relative expansion rate, and hence dark energy. While this technique is well-established in weak lensing, its application to strong lensing has traditionally focused on Double Source Plane Lenses (DSPLs). However, DSPLs are exceedingly rare and fundamentally limited by the Mass-Sheet Degeneracy (MSD), a systematic uncertainty underexplored in previous literature. To overcome these challenges, we introduce Pseudo Double-Source Plane Lenses (PDSPLs): pairs of independent single-source plane lenses with self-similar deflectors. This generalizes the DSPL formalism to the $\sim 10^5$ galaxy-galaxy lenses expected from LSST, Euclid, and Roman. Unlike true DSPLs, PDSPLs are free from the intermediate source mass problem by construction, eliminating the associated secondary MSD and the need for multi-plane ray tracing. We incorporate the deflector MSD into a hierarchical population model to forecast dark energy constraints in Flat $w_0w_a$CDM, showing that MSD severely degrades constraints from small DSPL samples and motivates our PDSPL statistical approach. Assuming unbiased Gaussian photo-z errors of $σ_z/(1+z)=0.03$, the mock LSST Y10 photometric sample yields $σ(w_0)\sim0.45$, constraining the population-mean MSD parameter and deflector power-law slope to $\sim2\%$. A prior $Ω_m\sim\mathcal{N}(0.3,0.05)$, representing combination with external cosmological probes such as CMB, BAO, or SNe Ia, improves this to $σ(w_0)\sim0.29$, comparable to Stage III weak lensing. The statistical advantage over smaller spectroscopic subsets (e.g., 4MOST) assumes unbiased photo-zs. Real-data use requires spectroscopic photo-z calibration and validation of how paired deflectors' mass-profile differences affect Einstein-radius ratios.

entry.title: Field analogue of the Ruijsenaars-Schneider model
entry.summary: We suggest a field extension of the classical elliptic Ruijsenaars-Schneider model. The model is defined in two different ways which lead to the same result. The first one is via the trace of a chain product of $L$-matrices which allows one to introduce the Hamiltonian of the model and to show that the model is gauge equivalent to a classical elliptic spin chain. In this way, one obtains a lattice field analogue of the Ruijsenaars-Schneider model with continuous time. The second method is based on investigation of general elliptic families of solutions to the 2D Toda equation. We derive equations of motion for their poles, which turn out to be difference equations in space with a lattice spacing $η$, together with a zero curvature representation for them. We also show that the equations of motion are Hamiltonian. The obtained system of equations can be naturally regarded as a field generalization of the Ruijsenaars-Schneider system. Its lattice version coincides with the model introduced via the first method. The limit $η\to 0$ is shown to give the field extension of the Calogero-Moser model known in the literature. The fully discrete version of this construction is also discussed.

entry.title: Phase transitions through excited-state level crossings and topological indicators: the case of the XXZ chain with staggered Ising interaction
entry.summary: We combine two ways of determining the phase diagram of the spin-$1/2$ XXZ chain with a staggered Ising interaction and uniform transverse exchange, based on exact diagonalization. The model realizes a competition between Néel order and bond-dimerized phases generated by the alternating Ising interaction. The simplest approach to determine the phase boundaries is to use topological indicators based on generalized position operators (GPOs). We show that in general, the bosonized and numerical results for the topological indicators agree. The second is the method of crossings of excited energy levels (MCEL), which is justified by conformal field theory. Despite the partial loss of translational symmetry induced by the alternating Ising interaction, we show that, with the aid of the GPO to identify the relevant level crossings, the MCEL provides an accurate determination of the phase boundary between the Néel and dimerized phases. While the jumps of a topological indicator based on a GPO provide a qualitatively correct phase diagram, its accuracy is affected when the gap is very small (or the correlation length very large) at one side of the transition, as we show using field-theoretical arguments. The combination of both methods provides a more efficient way of calculating phase diagrams for correlated one-dimensional models than other widely used conventional approaches.

entry.title: Spin-Induced Coordinate Noncommutativity of the Covariant Centroid
entry.summary: The Tulczyjew-Dixon centroid of a massive spinning particle, built as a composite of canonical Poincaré variables, carries the exact coordinate algebra $\{X^μ,X^ν\}=-S^{μν}/p^2$, whose noncommutativity bivector is the transverse spin tensor of the particle itself rather than an external background. That bracket and its Compton-scale magnitude are already known, and we recover them here as the starting point of the analysis, not as a result. What the composite realization settles is the domain on which the algebra may be used. Closure of the Jacobi identity requires $p^{-2}$ to remain operator valued, and the exactness domain is the convex timelike interior $Ω_μ$, on which states supported on a single mass shell are distributional. We show that freezing $p^2$ to its shell value inside the centroid leaves every two-operator commutator unchanged on shell, so that the projected position dictionary, the Berry cancellation and the endpoint transversality identity are untouched, while the same substitution fails from three insertions onward, with residue the truncated Jacobiator $2ε^{μνρσ}W_σ/(p^2)^2$. This two-versus-three criterion replaces the qualitative restriction to shell-preserving matrix elements and states which constructions built on a fixed-shell bivector $Θ_m$ remain valid. We then follow the algebra through positive-energy projection, packet-conditioned Moyal fibers, Compton routing holonomy and projected nonassociative products, recording for each layer whether it falls on the safe side of the criterion. No prediction beyond QED follows. In the geometric branch the physical amplitude reduces to the QED amplitude, and the transverse matching coefficients remain uncomputed.

entry.title: Transient X-ray Sources as Extremely Eccentric Mass-Transfer Binaries with Compact Companions
entry.summary: It has long been suggested that X-ray transients are produced at periastron of stellar-compact object binaries with eccentric orbits. Recoil of matter evaporated from the star by X-rays from matter transferred at periastron increases the orbital semi-major axis and eccentricity. After periastrons the object would be a transient X-ray source, a Galactic analogue of a tidal disruption event (TDE), but recurrent with a gradually increasing period rather than catastrophic.

entry.title: Black holes from a nonlocal equation of state: horizon geometry, singularity structure and thermodynamics
entry.summary: We show that a nonlocal equation of state for an anisotropic fluid reduces to a linear equation for the enclosed matter and uniquely selects a Yukawa-type density profile in a static, spherically symmetric Kerr--Schild geometry. The resulting neutral solution has finite-range hair, exponentially screened at large distances, with the asymptotic mass as its only conserved charge, and admits an exact horizon classification: horizonless configurations, Schwarzschild-like black holes, two-horizon geometries with a Cauchy horizon, and an extremal configuration whose mass and radius are obtained in closed form. We prove that the magnitude of the inner surface gravity exceeds that of the outer horizon throughout the two-horizon regime. When the central mass vanishes, the geometry approaches a global monopole in the static branch and a Kantowski--Sachs-type region in the nonstatic branch. The singularity satisfies Królak's strong-curvature criterion and is Tipler-strong along non-radial geodesics in the spacelike branch. For vanishing central mass, the Ricci scalar and the square root of the Kretschmann scalar are locally integrable with respect to the invariant spacetime volume, despite diverging at the origin. A power-law generalization of the nonlocal closure yields solutions expressed through incomplete gamma functions, interpolating between the singular core and a regular black hole with a de~Sitter core, without invoking nonlinear electrodynamics. We obtain closed-form surface gravities, an extended first-law identity and a Smarr relation, and locate the heat-capacity divergence using the lower branch of the Lambert function. Finally, thermodynamic topology distinguishes a Schwarzschild-like regime with one defect from an extremal regime with two opposite-winding defects that merge at the maximum Hawking temperature.

entry.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
entry.summary: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.

entry.title: Quantum-Relativistic Anomalous Proper Time
entry.summary: We investigate surprising consequences of the hypothesis that gravity and proper time obey the quantum superposition principle. We show that, for a massive body prepared in a superposition of two positions and post-selected in a suitable final state, the elapsed proper time in another region of space can assume an anomalous effective value lying outside the range allowed by classical general relativity. Remarkably, the effective elapsed proper time can even become negative, corresponding to an effective evolution backward in time. We also propose an experiment to observe an anomalous effective proper time associated with the internal degrees of freedom of a quantum particle in an interferometer under Earth's gravitational field. The proposed experiment is, in principle, feasible with current technology, and its realization could provide the first experimental evidence of an interplay between quantum mechanics and general relativity beyond the effects of the Newtonian potential in flat spacetime.

entry.title: Constraining Twin-Star Existence in Four-Parameter Maxwell Equation of State
entry.summary: Twin stars (TSs) are predicted to exist in nature if the hadron-to-quark phase transition is strong enough to form a new branch of hybrid stars, separated from the branch of neutron stars. It is essential to study the hybrid equation of states (EoSs) that can form TSs, with a primary focus on estimating the onset of the phase transition and its strength. We systematically study the TS scenario by adopting a four-parameter Maxwell-CSS approach to construct a large ensemble of Maxwell-type hybrid EoSs. Within this framework, we report the conditions on our parameter space imposed by the TOV solutions. For a fixed transition energy density and speed of sound for quark matter, we define distinct ranges of transition pressures based on the allowed strengths of discontinuity. Below a maximum transition pressure, a range of discontinuity exists that increases as the transition pressure decreases. Thereby, we identify the loci of the limits on discontinuities as the TS existence boundaries. Based on the causality limit, the TS existence boundaries can be truncated. Strong constraints on this picture are drawn from the CET, GW170817 and NICER. Within our considered model, we computed conditional extrema surviving the adopted $2σ$ filters---the maximum mass for TSs to be $2.05~M_\odot$, the allowed strongest discontinuity in rest-mass density to be $7.76ρ_\mathrm{sat}$, and the upper bound on transition rest-mass density to be $4.03ρ_\mathrm{sat}$. Subsequently, we compute the implications of the stiffness of the quark matter EoS on this picture. Different confidence levels for observational constraints are considered to assess the extent to which Maxwell-type EOSs remain compatible with the observations.

entry.title: Cooperation of itinerant and localized physics in the magnetic phase diagram of 214 Ruddlesden-Popper iridates
entry.summary: The $5d^5$ Ruddlesden-Popper iridates Sr$_2$IrO$_4$ and Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ have attracted considerable attention as spin-orbit entangled analogues of the cuprates, yet the origin of their antiferromagnetic insulating state, of Slater or of Mott-Heisenberg type, remains debated. We find that both materials sit in an intermediate regime in which itinerant and localized electrons cooperate in stabilizing the antiferromagnetic order, with Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ slightly more correlated than Sr$_2$IrO$_4$. We obtain this by computing, within dynamical mean-field theory, the interaction-temperature phase diagram of a realistic three-orbital $t_{2g}$ Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling. Our study shows that neither the behavior of the gap across the Néel temperature nor the spin-polaron features of the spectral function unambiguously identify the cooperative regime, whereas the two-peak structure of the optical conductivity is reproduced only there and therefore constitutes a reliable fingerprint. By placing both compounds in a common phase diagram, our results reconcile seemingly contradictory experimental and theoretical reports, and provide a unified framework for future studies of the 214 iridates and of other spin-orbit coupled correlated materials.

entry.title: Environmental dependence of galaxy properties in the southern GAMA regions
entry.summary: Using data from the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) survey, we investigate how galaxy properties correlate with the local environment, focusing on its two southern regions (G02 and G23) that have not previously been examined in this context. We employ two-point and marked correlation functions to quantify the environmental dependence of galaxy color, stellar mass, luminosity across the $u$, $g$, $r$, $J$, and $K$ bands, as well as star formation rate (SFR) and specific star formation rate (sSFR). Our results show that $u-r$ and $g-r$ colors are most strongly correlated with local overdensity, followed by stellar mass. The SFR and sSFR exhibit a clear inverse relationship with environmental density, consistent with the trend observed for $u$-band luminosity, which traces young stellar populations. The galaxies brighter in the $g$, $J$, and $K$ bands preferentially inhabit denser regions. We interpret the environmental dependence of color using Halo Occupation Distribution (HOD) modeling. The HOD modeling indicates that red galaxies trace dense environments more strongly than blue galaxies, exhibiting significantly higher satellite fractions and occupying more massive halos. We demonstrate that both redshift and stellar mass incompleteness systematically affect clustering measurements, generally enhancing the observed environmental dependence. Comparing our measurements from the southern regions with those from the equatorial GAMA regions, we find that the overall environmental trends remain consistent. The measured correlations provide key constraints for models of galaxy assembly across mass and environment, while environmental trends in color and near-infrared luminosity trace stellar mass growth and quenching with redshift.

entry.title: A unified dark sector from a single canonical scalar field in Bohmian Wheeler-DeWitt cosmology with a cuscuton-inspired potential
entry.summary: We quantize a spatially flat FLRW minisuperspace containing one canonical scalar field with the hyperbolic potential generated by a cuscuton-type superpotential, and extract cosmological histories from the Wheeler-DeWitt wave function in the de Broglie-Bohm interpretation. For the canonical potential parameter, related to the original cuscuton couplings, below an explicit critical value the potential has a unique nondegenerate minimum with positive height, and the ratio $κ$ of the scalar mass to the de Sitter Hubble rate at the minimum diverges as $κ^2\simeq 3b/δ$, where $δ$ is the relative distance to criticality. For the original hyperbolic potential, $κ\leq 3/\sqrt{2}$, whereas its cuscuton-inspired generalization allows a large hierarchy between scalar oscillation and expansion rates. For $κ\gg1$, small excitation and sufficiently large cell action, the reduced wave equation has an adiabatic Gaussian solution describing a de Sitter vacuum, a classical oscillating condensate whose averaged excitation density redshifts as $a^{-3}$, and, at the packet centre, a leading quantum density equal to the zero-point energy of the effective homogeneous oscillator divided by the physical cell volume, which is also dust-like. Full numerical solutions of the Wheeler-DeWitt equation support the averaged zero-point law at the reported $10^{-3}$ level, reproduce its dependence on the position of the Bohmian particle inside the packet, show that quantum corrections to the present Hubble rate converge as the inverse of the cell action, and support a single-field dust-plus-vacuum description at the homogeneous background level when $κ\gg1$. The classical histories approach the $Λ$CDM distance relations with a deviation of $1.3/κ$ in $D_V$. The dark energy component has $w=-1$ by construction, and the model is not fitted to data.

entry.title: The SIRMOS mission concept: a space-based near-IR spectroscopic survey of 100 million galaxies in the Euclid Wide Survey footprint
entry.summary: SIRMOS is a mission concept for a future NASA Astrophysics Explorer opportunity that aims to revolutionize our understanding of the universe by mapping the large-scale structure of galaxies in unprecedented breadth and detail to explore cosmic origins and evolution. Specifically, the primary science goals of SIRMOS are to discover how cosmic inflation seeded large-scale structure, reveal the nature of the accelerating expansion of the universe, and measure the sum of neutrino masses to exceptionally high precision. Its secondary science goals include determining how environment shapes galaxy evolution at cosmic noon and beyond, and probing the Milky Way's dust-enshrouded regions, reaching the far side of our Galaxy. To accomplish its transformative science goals, SIRMOS executes a 3-year cosmology survey over the Euclid footprint of ~14,000 deg$^2$, obtaining slit spectra for ~100 million galaxies at 1<z<4. SIRMOS is the first space mission designed specifically to leverage Euclid's wide near-infrared (IR) imaging survey for target selection and employs a digital micro-mirror device (DMD) to acquire up to 4,000 simultaneous spectra over a wide 0.9 deg$^2$ field of view. The instrument's excellent spectral resolution of $R=1300$ and continuous wavelength coverage from 1.25--2.5 $μ$m capture the redshifts of distant galaxies with no gaps, reducing systematic biases to achieve ground-breaking science.

entry.title: The Free Scalar as a Thermal Envelope for Three-Dimensional CFTs
entry.summary: We conjecture that every unitary three-dimensional conformal field theory obeys $c_S/C_T\leq16πζ(3)$, where $s=c_ST^2$ is the thermal entropy density and $C_T$ the stress-tensor two-point coefficient, with equality for free scalars. We embed this in a stronger conjecture: on $S^1\times H^2$, the $C_T$-normalized hyperbolic heat capacity is bounded above by that of the free scalar for all $T\geq(2πR)^{-1}$. Near the conformal temperature, for theories smooth from the high-temperature side and without boundary terms in the modular Hamiltonian, the heat-capacity bound follows from conformal-collider positivity. We test the conjectures in free, interacting large-$N$, and holographic theories. Monte Carlo data for the three-dimensional Ising and $O(N)$ models also obey the flat-space bound.

entry.title: Hybrid Partial Dressing: Correct Effective Potentials at All Temperatures
entry.summary: We develop Hybrid Partial Dressing (HPD), a simple diagrammatic resummation scheme for finite-temperature effective potentials in scalar field theory which is valid at all temperatures. HPD improves on earlier resummation schemes such as Daisy Resummation and Partial Dressing by being two-loop exact at all temperatures and free of the overlapping momentum problem. Renormalization group improvement is straightforward to implement. We illustrate the scheme in multi-scalar theories with a spontaneously broken $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry, and compare it against existing approaches, showing in particular that it reproduces the two-loop Dimensional Reduction (DR) potential exactly in the high-temperature regime where DR applies, while remaining valid at all temperatures. This makes HPD suitable for the general study of strong first order phase transitions beyond the Standard Model, as we demonstrate through gravitational wave predictions from HPD and its RG-improved version, RGHPD.

entry.title: Construction of holomorphic SCFTs with minimal index
entry.summary: It has been an open question whether there exist holomorphic VOAs with N=1 supersymmetry and Witten index 1 for any positive central charge c. The existence of such a theory with c=288 is closely related to the 576-periodicity of the TMF spectrum via the Segal-Stolz-Teichner conjecture. Here we report the construction of thousands of such theories by extending the approach initiated by Gaiotto and Johnson-Freyd via ternary codes. In addition, for every positive integer k, we also construct holomorphic N=1 VOAs of central charge c=12k with index 24/gcd(24,k) -- conjectured to be the minimum -- in a computer-aided search carried out by AI coding agents. We overcome the exponential-time barrier by using chains of smaller cells to build ternary codes, whose indices can then be evaluated via a transfer-matrix technique, and we use a symmetric orbifold construction to reduce the problem of k=12 and 24 to that of k=6. Along the way, we also establish several results on ternary codes and their indices. Using an observation relating codes and Landau-Ginzburg orbifold models, we argue that the non-chiral doubles of the ternary code VOAs can always be gapped supersymmetrically.

entry.title: The Hosts and Mass Distribution Function of the Most Massive Black Holes: Implications for the nHz Gravitational Wave Background
entry.summary: We use the core-radius, $r_γ,$ of a galaxy's central core along with a volume-limited sample of brightest cluster galaxies (BCG) to determine the $z=0$ mass distribution function of the most massive super-massive black holes (SMBH). We recover a $M_{BH}-r_γ$ relationship between the SMBH mass, $M_{BH},$ and $r_γ$ of form $M_{BH} \approx1.3\times10^{10}~(r_γ/{\mathrm{kpc}})~M_\odot,$ with $σ= 0.25\pm0.03$ dex scatter in $M_{BH}.$ We derive a core distribution function (CDF), based on HST and DLS images of the BCGs. The CDF falls steeply as $N(r_γ)\sim r_γ^{-3}$ for $r_γ>0.50$ kpc. Only $\sim5\%$ of BCGs have $r_γ>1$ kpc. Combining the CDF and $M_{BH} - r_γ$ relationship yields the BH mass distribution function (MDF). For $M_{BH} \geq 7\times10^{9}~\mathrm{M_\odot}$ (the mean $M_{BH}$ at $r_γ=0.50$ kpc) we derive: $\log\left(\frac{dN(M_{BH})}{d{M_{BH}/10^{10} M_\odot}}~[\rm Mpc^{-3}]\right)=(-3.05\pm0.42)~\log\left(\frac{M_{BH}}{10^{10}M_\odot}\right)~-~5.11\ (+0.41, -0.36)$. Cores with $r_γ\geq 0.50$ kpc are found almost exclusively in BCGs, implying that SMBHs with $M_{BH} \geq7\times10^{9}~\mathrm{M_\odot}$ may also be exclusive to BCGs. Core-radius correlates with $α,$ a parameter that characterizes the growth of BCG envelopes by mergers, suggesting that the most massive SMBHs grew in tandem with their BCG hosts. The BH MDF embodies a significant population of SMBH with $M_{BH} >7\times10^{9} M_\odot.$ When combined with the Liepold & Ma (2024) BH MDF to account for SMBH with $M_{BH} < 7\times10^{9} M_\odot,$ it can comfortably explain the nHz gravitational wave background.

entry.title: SN Ares: A Strongly Lensed Type IIb Supernova at $\mathbf{z=1.276}$ with a Predicted 70-Year Time Delay
entry.summary: We present the discovery of supernova (SN) Ares, a strongly lensed supernova at $z_{\rm spec}=1.276\pm0.002$ in a massive, triply imaged host galaxy behind the MACS J0308.9+2645 galaxy cluster. JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy spanning the rest-frame optical to NIR of Ares reveals helium features at $5876\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, $7065\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, and $10830\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, as well as H$α$ and Pa$β$. A comparison to local core-collapse SN spectra and light curves leads to a classification of SN Ares as a Type IIb supernova, the highest-redshift member of its class spectroscopically identified. A comparison to local SN IIb light curves provides a phase estimate for the spectrum of $34_{-9}^{+10}$ rest-frame days post-radioactive peak, providing a unique view into a high-redshift stripped-envelope supernova in its late-photospheric evolution. A lens model of the cluster constructed using recent JWST data indicates that SN Ares is the first image to arrive and will reappear in two future images near the center of the cluster plane in $\gtrsim 70$ years, with predicted magnifications of $\sim5\times$ and $\sim1.5\times$. Planned JWST/NIRSpec Multi-Object Spectroscopy of the cluster will allow for more detailed modeling of the lensed system for tighter constraints on the time delay and magnifications, as well as a template spectrum at the location of SN Ares.

entry.title: $El\ Ascua$: An ultra-luminous, radio-loud, Compton-thick AGN at $z\sim 3.8$ hiding in plain sight revealed by MINERVA multi-band MIRI observations
entry.summary: Heavily dust-obscured active galactic nuclei (AGN) are crucial for understanding supermassive black hole growth. Using multi-band MIRI photometry from the MINERVA survey, we report the discovery in the UDS field of an extremely mid-infrared bright Compton-thick AGN (CT AGN) at $z \sim 3.8$, \textit{el Ascua} (the Ember). The AGN and/or its host galaxy is detected at 870\,$μ$m with ALMA and at 1.4\,GHz with the VLA. With UV-to-radio spectral energy distribution modeling, we estimate that the dusty host galaxy has a stellar mass of $\log\left( M_\star / M_\odot \right)=10.82 \pm 0.57$ and a star formation rate of ${\rm{SFR}} =157 \pm 8 \,M_\odot\,{\rm yr^{-1}}$, and we confirm the presence of a powerful dusty AGN with an intrinsic accretion luminosity of $\log\left( L_{\rm{acc}} /{\rm erg\,s^{-1}} \right)=47.12 \pm 0.58$. CT obscuration is revealed by comparing the upper limit on the X-ray luminosity over $2-10 \,{\rm{keV}}$ with the $6 \,{\rmμ{m}}$ mid-IR AGN luminosity. We additionally find evidence for a radio excess by comparing its total IR-to-radio ratio to those of typical star-forming galaxies and radio-quiet AGN, implying that \textit{el Ascua} could be a rare radio-loud CT AGN. With an extremely high ratio between black hole accretion rate and SFR, the AGN is likely nearing the peak of a deeply obscured phase of black hole growth before AGN feedback blows away the obscuring material. Our work demonstrates the power of MIRI to reveal heavily obscured AGN missing from our supermassive black hole census.

entry.title: Dark Matter and MOND successes and degeneracies in reproducing SPARC rotation curves and weak lensing data
entry.summary: The observed rotation velocities of spiral galaxies at large scales exceed those predicted by their baryonic components, motivating the need for dark matter (DM) or Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND). We fit the rotation curves of 147 late-type galaxies from the SPARC database, using a suite of models including Cold Dark Matter (CDM) models with and without baryonic feedback, Warm DM, Fuzzy DM, and MOND. We also combine SPARC kinematics with weak-lensing data to extend the mean rotation curves to ~1 Mpc. On a galaxy-by-galaxy basis, the inner SPARC rotation curves marginally favour CDM models with baryonic feedback, although accounting for the uncertainties in distances and inclinations increases the degeneracy among DM-based models and MOND. All DM models predict host halo masses larger than abundance-matching expectations, with only the CDM model with baryonic feedback reducing the scatter around the mean luminosity-halo mass relation. MOND is able to reproduce the flatness of the mean galactic rotation curves on scales up to 1 Mpc, providing stellar mass-to-light ratios within observational uncertainties. In contrast, all DM models, without the contribution of mass external to the bound halo, struggle to explain the flat rotation curves. The inclusion of the current weak-lensing data tends to favour MOND over DM models, at least at the largest scales. Future observations from BIG-SPARC, the Square Kilometre Array, and most importantly, upcoming weak-lensing surveys such as EUCLID and Rubin will provide more stringent and independent tests of these competing frameworks

entry.title: Direct tests of conformal symmetry with Rydberg atoms: assessment and proposals
entry.summary: We propose a direct test of conformal symmetry using Rydberg-atom arrays. By arranging the atoms on a circle and measuring equal-time two-point correlation functions, the characteristic functional form predicted by conformal field theory can be tested directly. We estimate the number of experimental snapshots required to resolve this behavior with sufficient statistical precision. We further optimize the time-dependent ramp profile of the Rabi frequency~$Ω$ and detuning~$Δ$ used to prepare the target critical state adiabatically. The optimized profile achieves higher fidelity over much shorter evolution times than those employed in previous experiments. Taken together, these results suggest that a direct experimental test of conformal symmetry is feasible with current Rydberg-atom technology.

entry.title: A Low Scale for Quark-Lepton Unification
entry.summary: The measured fermion masses may be pointing to the scale of quark-lepton unification. Studying the renormalization-group evolution of the Standard Model Yukawa couplings, we find that $y_τ=y_b$ and $y_μ=3y_s$ occur at nearly the same scale, around $10^6$ GeV, while the first generation reaches the Georgi-Jarlskog relation $y_e\simeq y_d/3$ at order $10^8$ GeV and can arise from the same Clebsch structure through a simple hierarchical flavor texture. This pattern naturally suggests low-scale Pati-Salam symmetry. We show that flavor mixing and finite threshold corrections preserve this picture. If the electron mass has an independent origin, the two heavier-generation relations can be realized in theories with a unification scale as low as $(5$-$7)\times10^5$ GeV. We identify two simple theories that accommodate all three relations and in which the measured masses fix the flavor structure. The first unifies all three generations at $4.6^{+1.2}_{-0.9}\times10^6$ GeV; the second, with symmetric Yukawa matrices, at $1.5^{+0.7}_{-0.5}\times10^7$ GeV, and predicts $|V_{cb}|=0.042\pm0.002$. Their shared light-family texture fixes the relevant vector-leptoquark couplings, making $μ\to e$ conversion in nuclei a direct test of unification: upcoming searches will probe part of the region selected by the two theories, and proposed facilities could cover it completely.

entry.title: Dark Matter phase space distribution under a fully relativistic treatment. Eddington inversion according to general relativity
entry.summary: We develop a fully relativistic extension of Eddington inversion to reconstruct the phase-space distribution function of dark matter from its density profile. Treating dark matter as an effective perfect fluid in a static, spherically symmetric spacetime, we use the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations to determine the gravitational background and derive an Abel-type inversion that yields the distribution function in terms of the conserved particle energy measured at infinity. We show that the resulting expression recovers the classical Eddington inversion in the weak-field, nonrelativistic limit. We also investigate the finite-boundary contribution, which can introduce an unphysical divergence, and present a regularization procedure that removes it. We apply our method to a Milky Way model consisting of a generalized Navarro-Frenk-White halo and a Gondolo-Silk dark-matter spike around Sagittarius A$^*$, neglecting baryonic contributions. The relativistic and Newtonian velocity distributions agree at radii far from the Galactic center but begin to differ at distances of order $10^{-5}\,\mathrm{pc}$. Closer to the black hole, the relativistic peak speed can reach approximately twice the Newtonian prediction. Finally, we derive a general expression for dark-matter capture by neutron stars that accommodates arbitrary ambient velocity distributions. Near Sagittarius A$^*$, the relativistic capture factor is nearly an order of magnitude smaller than the Maxwell-Boltzmann prediction, while the Newtonian Eddington result can overestimate it by a factor of approximately two. These results demonstrate the importance of relativistic phase-space reconstruction for dark-matter phenomenology in strong gravitational fields.

entry.title: One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres-Douglas
entry.summary: We propose a uniform construction of affine schemes encoding the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(ADE)$, with $\gcd(p,h^\vee)=1$. The construction captures conjectural OPE decoupling relations via the Jacobian ring of a single invariant polynomial potential, obtained from a polynomial twisted period of the corresponding Coxeter orbit space. We show that these potentials are ``syzygy-maximizing'' in the first jet schemes and recover the Higgs branches as their reduced critical loci. We obtain closed determinant expressions for the classical types and explicit potentials for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$. Powers of the nilradical define an intrinsic filtration on the resulting Jacobian rings, from which we compute candidate Macdonald indices with the correct Schur and Hall--Littlewood limits, in the examples studied. Restricting the potentials to Slodowy slices extends the prescription to nilpotently Higgsed theories. We further conjecture that these Jacobian rings are isomorphic to Zhu's $C_2$-algebras of simple affine VOAs at boundary admissible levels and their quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reductions.
